budget_items.what_was_said: The assessing office processed a commitment of motor vehicle excise bills for the month; the warrant was signed April 22nd.
One additional bill was issued under this commitment number.
64 motor vehicle excise abatements were received and processed in the past month, awaiting payment by the tax collector.
All FY2026 real estate abatements have been processed; some granted, some denied including personal property/sole company items.
Supplemental real estate bills were prepared for three properties whose building value increased more than 50%, based on occupancy date.

The principal assessor gave an update on progress toward the town's new-growth estimate, noting the commercial/industrial figure so far and the equivalent tax bill value; said they may fall a bit short but remain in range.

budget_items.topic: Vision printing of CAI-style property cards
budget_items.what_was_said: A quote was given for Vision to print updated property cards annually instead of doing it in-house, proposed for next year.
A vendor quote was cited for continuously updating GIS layers such as catch basin data, discussed in context of townwide use of the CI/GIS platform.
The board signed and voted to approve the notice of commitment covering the three supplemental bills discussed earlier.
The chair reminded seniors of the circuit breaker tax credit and means-tested exemption, and noted the interest rate that applies if taxes are deferred.

decisions.decision: Board leaned toward keeping both the fixed annual Vision property card (as of January 1) and a CI-based card updated monthly, clearly labeled as to which is which.
Job posting language to be revised to require experience specifically in the assessing field, not just appraisal, and to add computer/CAMA/Munis/Microsoft Suite skills to qualifications.
Job posting/description to require current MAA designation or achievement of it within two years of hire.
Job description language changed from the assessor 'recommends' the tax rate to something like 'presents/estimates tax rate options,' since the assessor does not set the rate.
Add 'deferrals' alongside abatements and exemptions in the job description's duties list.
Narrow 'maintains the town's official maps' to specifically 'tax maps' in the job description.
Board intends to bring cyclical property inspections in-house going forward rather than continue contracting them out.
Next Board of Assessors meeting set for June 3rd.

minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed the principal assessor's monthly activity report (excise commitments, abatements, supplemental bills, GIS/server issues) and discussed how to reconcile the fixed annual Vision property card with a more frequently updated CI-based card. With principal assessor Linda departing at the end of June, the board line-edited a draft job posting and description for her replacement, emphasizing assessing (not just appraisal) experience and technology skills, and discussed pulling contracted services such as cyclical inspections back in-house. The board also received a detailed update on a neighborhood/waterfront reclassification project, recommended against the town purchasing a foreclosed Hollis Road property, and set the next meeting for June 3rd before adjourning to executive session.

what_happened.line: Board line-edited the principal assessor job posting and description ahead of Linda's end-of-June departure, adding assessing (not just appraisal) experience and technology requirements.
Board signaled intent to bring cyclical property inspections in-house rather than continue contracting them out.
Board voted, stated unanimous, to recommend the town not purchase a foreclosed property on Hollis Road.
Board leaned toward keeping both the annual Vision property card and a more frequently updated CI-based card, clearly labeled as to which is which.
Next Board of Assessors meeting set for June 3rd.

why_it_matters: The principal assessor's office sets property valuations that underlie every resident's tax bill, so how the replacement is hired and qualified matters directly.
Moving inspections in-house is a change to how the assessing office operates and could affect its staffing or contracted-services budget.
The Hollis Road recommendation is a vote the Select Board or Town will act on regarding town acquisition of a foreclosed property.
